University of Sistan and Baluchestan, Zahedan
Extreme Light Infrastructure Nuclear Physics
(IFIN-HN), Magurele
3 MV Van de Graaff accelerator
Two LiF targets with natural isotopic composition
were prepared using the physical vapor deposition
technique by evaporating high-purity anhydrous LiF
powder onto self-supporting Ag and C layer.
For the LiF/Ag target, a self-supporting Ag layer with
a thickness of (1235+/-50)x10**15 atom/cm2 and an area
of 65 mm2.
For the Au/LiF/C target, the self-supporting C layer
consisted of a diamond-like carbon (DLC) film with a
nominal thickness of 100 ug/cm2. A thin Au film was
deposited onto the LiF layer.
P-type detector with a 213 cm3 crystal placed at
90 degree relative to the beam axis, nominal
efficiency of 50% and resolution of ~4 keV for
1.33 MeV gamma-ray from a 60Co source.
Ion-implanted Si detector (25 mm2 area, 300 um
active depth) 30 keV energy resolution was placed at a
backward angle of 165 degree for the detection of
scattered particles.
Rutherford-scattered protons from Ag(or Au)
were used to determine the number of incident protons.
